### Don’t Use Sex as a Weapon - Crosswalk Couples Devotional - May 3
Author: Michelle S. Lazurek
Site: Crosswalk.com
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-couples-devotional/dont-use-sex-as-a-weapon-crosswalk-couples-devotional-may-3.html
Passage: 1 Corinthians 7:5
Points:
- Spouses may feel tempted to withhold physical intimacy when feeling emotionally neglected or unloved.
- Withholding sexual intimacy as a weapon or bargaining chip damages the relationship and invites temptation.
- Scripture permits abstaining from intimacy only by mutual agreement for a temporary season of prayer.
- Believers must look to Christ rather than their spouse for ultimate, unconditional love and fulfillment.
- Regularly giving to one another in marriage protects the covenant and guards against outside temptation.

### Conjugal Rights in Marriage
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/conjugal-rights-in-marriage
Passage: 1 Corinthians 7:3-5
Points:
- Scripture affirms marital intimacy as holy and good, not merely a concession for procreation.
- Both husband and wife share mutual obligations and rights to enjoy intimacy together.
- Surrendering authority over one’s body does not justify abusive, demeaning, or sinful demands.
- Spouses should avoid abstaining from intimacy without a legitimate mutual reason, such as prayer or illness.
- Navigating physical intimacy requires ongoing wisdom, respect, and mutual self-giving.

### Sexual Intimacy and the Rights over a Spouse’s Body in Marriage
Author: John Piper
Site: Desiring God
URL: https://www.desiringgod.org/articles/sexual-intimacy-and-the-rights-over-a-spouses-body-in-marriage
Passage: 1 Corinthians 7:3-5
Points:
- Mutual authority over each other’s body creates a real-world paradox that strict logic cannot resolve.
- Paul's words do not give either spouse a license to demand acts that the other finds distressing.
- Husbands and wives are called to outdo one another in showing honor rather than enforcing demands.
- Biblical husbandly leadership leads by seeking to maximize the wife's well-being and pleasure.
- Self-sacrificing grace breaks stalemates by finding joy in giving rather than merely receiving.
